solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rapidly changing US port

definitions.meaning: a face or situation that alters quickly is described this way
the Gulf Coast city in Alabama

explanation.surface: A description of an American harbour town whose fortunes shift quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the adjective for something that moves or alters readily, and the Alabama seaport of that name.

clue.text: Get high on it for a short time before regularly taking crack

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a brief time
to be on a medicine is to take it regularly
to have a crack at something is to have a shot at it

explanation.surface: Reads like a slangy warning about a brief binge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' means an attempt, not anything illicit. The definition is playful: a rocket sent to the Moon gets very high.
explanation.definitionFit: A launch aimed at the Moon goes higher than almost anything, so the whole phrase describes it cryptically.

clue.text: Dance star following manager to Australia

indicators.note: following places the star after the manager and Australia

parts.note: a boss is a manager
A is the international vehicle code for Australia
a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: A dancing celebrity who moved to Australia after their manager.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brazilian style of music and the dance performed to it, a type of dance.

clue.text: Act without restraint in rental property near Split

parts.note: in Britain a let is a property rented out
a rip is a split or tear

explanation.surface: Wild behaviour in a holiday flat close to Split, the Croatian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' looks like the Croatian port but means a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to behave or speak freely with no holding back.

clue.text: Overjoyed by quote about taking in abandoned cats

indicators.note: taking in says the turned word holds the scrambled letters inside it
about tells us the word for quote is turned round

parts.note: to quote a source is to cite it

indicators.note: abandoned, in the sense of wild and unrestrained, signals the letters of cats are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled by a remark about rescuing cats that were left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' looks like it describes the cats' plight, but it signals the jumble; the inserted letters go just after the first letter of the turned word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe a state of intense delight; they are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Agreeing with second report revised to include Norway

indicators.note: to include means the anagram takes in the letter for Norway
revised says the letters of second report are reworked

parts.note: N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: A second report has been rewritten to cover Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges SECOND REPORT, and 'to include' slips N into the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Corresponding means matching or in agreement, as figures that correspond.

clue.text: Set off with 26 Germans on board

indicators.note: on board means the Germans are carried inside the other word

parts.note: the number points to the answer to 26 across, the judge
G is the abbreviation for German, so two of them make GG

explanation.surface: A judge sets off with some Germans as passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: '26' stands for that answer, TRIER, which holds GG 'on board'.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off an alarm or reaction is to cause it to start, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Right about excellent mounting on American's jewelled headband

indicators.note: mounting, in a down clue, means the letters read upwards
about means the right abbreviation goes round the letters for excellent

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: An American's fine jewelled headband, properly set in its mount.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 meaning first-rate is written AI in crosswords. In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the American letter comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled ornamental coronet worn on the head, such as one a princess wears at a ball.

clue.text: Cunning Brexiteer speaking in support of Chequers at first

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means sitting underneath, so this piece follows
at first asks for the opening letter of Chequers
speaking means the word is said aloud, giving a soundalike

parts.note: a Brexiteer voted Leave in the 2016 UK referendum, so is a leaver

explanation.surface: A sly Leave campaigner speaking in favour of Chequers, the 2018 Brexit plan.
explanation.walkthrough: Chequers was Theresa May's 2018 Brexit plan, named after the Prime Minister's country house.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone sharp-witted and ingenious, adjective synonyms.

clue.text: About to prepare for an attack

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject
to set a table or trap is to prepare it

explanation.surface: An army readying itself to launch an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: The beginning of an illness can be called an attack, as in a sudden attack of fever.

clue.text: Develop a way to check the origin of merchandise entering Ireland

indicators.note: to check is to hold back or contain, so the gate holds the rest inside it

parts.note: a gate is a way in or out

indicators.note: entering puts the first letter of merchandise inside the name for Ireland

parts.note: Erin is a poetic name for Ireland

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A customs procedure for verifying where imported goods come from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'check' here means restrain or hold in, which is why it signals containment; 'a way' as a whole is the word for an opening in a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A seed that sprouts starts to grow, so the verb means to develop or begin to grow.

clue.text: When everyone's out of kilter knight agrees to change

indicators.note: to change says the letters of the fodder are altered into a new order

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A disordered knight agrees to make changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of kilter' looks like a phrase, but 'out' ends the definition and 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage by workers across all industries means everyone downs tools, a nationwide walkout.

clue.text: Calling for volunteers at end of event in Swiss town

indicators.note: in places the volunteers and the letter inside the town's name

parts.note: Sion is a town in the Valais canton of Switzerland
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: An appeal for helpers at the close of an event held in Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time volunteer soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: One's station in life is one's rank or occupation, close to a calling or vocation.

clue.text: Extremely vulnerable after English soldiers make chase

indicators.note: after says the extreme letters of vulnerable come second, following the English soldiers

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extreme letters, the first and last, of vulnerable

explanation.surface: Exposed troops from England are made to give pursuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the outer letters VE at the end; 'make' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: In metalwork, to chase is to decorate a surface by cutting or embossing designs, a craft sense of carving.

clue.text: Former pupil starts to object even as it's played

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil of a school

indicators.note: starts to asks for the first letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: An old boy objects even while something is being played.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodwind instrument is something that is played, so the phrase defines it loosely by function.

clue.text: Characteristic of possessions collectively

definitions.meaning: everything someone owns, taken as a whole

explanation.surface: A descriptive note about belongings taken as a group.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an attribute of something and the things a person owns.

clue.text: Standard in vehicle set up with gear changing device

indicators.note: set up, in a down clue, means the word reads upwards

parts.note: a dray is a low cart used by brewers
a gear stick changes a car's gears

explanation.surface: A car fitted out with a standard gear stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure against which others are judged is a benchmark or standard.

clue.text: Risk finding padre cavorting with Joy

indicators.note: cavorting, leaping about, signals the letters dance into a new order

explanation.surface: A priest larking about with a woman called Joy is courting scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in danger of loss or harm is to be at risk, so the noun means peril.

clue.text: Seabird circling cold region somewhere in New Zealand

indicators.note: circling means the bird's name goes round the letter for cold

parts.note: the auk is a diving seabird of northern waters
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a land is a region or country

explanation.surface: A seabird wheeling over a chilly part of New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest city of New Zealand, on the North Island, is one specific place there.

clue.text: Vexed by Jesse oddly missing with punches

parts.note: to be cross is to be vexed or annoyed

indicators.note: oddly missing means the odd-placed letters of Jesse are dropped, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: A boxer annoyed by Jesse, who keeps throwing and missing.
explanation.definitionFit: In boxing, a blow thrown across the body over the opponent's lead is a named type of punch.

clue.text: Unattached and available

definitions.meaning: not tied or committed to anything
not busy, as in having time to spare

explanation.surface: A dating profile: single and ready to meet someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both loose or not fastened and not otherwise engaged.

clue.text: Peto absorbed in Welshman's poems

indicators.note: absorbed in means the setter is taken inside the name

parts.note: Rhys is a typical Welsh man's name
Peto is the setter, who refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: The setter Peto is engrossed in a Welsh poet's verses.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter naming themself stands for ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Short pieces of verse are often called this, as in nursery verses.

clue.text: Only some remember that old lace collar

indicators.note: Only some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A reminder to keep in mind only part of an old piece of lacework.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep falling collar of lace on a Victorian dress was a fashion item with this name.

clue.text: Chinese scepticism reported by charity

indicators.note: reported means the phrase is said aloud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Han is the main ethnic group of China, and doubt is scepticism

explanation.surface: Doubts in China are being written up by an aid organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: HAN DOUBT spoken sounds like the answer, since the B in the second word is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift of money or food to someone in need is an act of charity, an alms.

clue.text: Defenceless king strangled by cleric from behind

indicators.note: from behind means the result is read backwards
this means the king is gripped tightly inside the word for the cleric

parts.note: a dean is a senior cleric
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A historical plot: an unguarded monarch overpowered by a churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: K inside DEAN gives DEKAN, and 'from behind' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unclothed or unprotected leaves one exposed, so the adjective means vulnerable.

clue.text: Settles for just less eventually in court

parts.note: even means fair or just, as in an even contest

indicators.note: eventually points to what comes in the end, the last letter of less

parts.note: to be up before a judge is to be in court

explanation.surface: Someone accepts a lower payout at the end of a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: To square a debt or score is to settle it, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Result in dress being thrown together

parts.note: to make something happen is to result in it
a shift is a loose straight dress

explanation.surface: A dress that turns out to have been hastily assembled.
explanation.definitionFit: Something improvised from whatever is at hand has been hastily assembled, a temporary stopgap.

clue.text: Writer distraught after wife leaves for judge

indicators.note: distraught, very upset, signals the remaining letters are thrown into disorder
leaves means the letter for wife departs from writer

explanation.surface: An author left upset when his wife walks out turns to a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes W from WRITER, leaving RITER, which 'distraught' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tries a case in court hears and decides it, so the word names a judge.

clue.text: Avoid in part backing favourites

parts.note: a side is one part of something, such as one part of a dispute

indicators.note: backing means the word is turned round, read from back to front

parts.note: pets are favourites, as in a teacher's pets

explanation.surface: Supporting favourites, at least partly, as a gambler might.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge a question or a tackle is to evade it, a figurative step aside.

clue.text: Footman's deficiency Pepys regularly ignored

parts.note: a lack is a shortage or deficiency

indicators.note: regularly ignored means every other letter of the diarist's name is dropped, keeping the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A servant's shortcoming that the diarist Samuel Pepys habitually overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Pepys was a 17th-century English diarist; skipping P, P and S leaves E and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A liveried servant or flunkey; the word is a synonym for a manservant who waits on others.
